correctness.rationale: A complete Fano incidence case analysis bounds dissociation size by seven, classifies the 58 optimum configurations and proves that A_T is one-token adjacent to B_U exactly when T and U are disjoint nonline triples. The extra exchanged line and point are incident, so all optimal jumps are slides. The standard Fano triple construction identifies the mobile component with the bipartite double of Coxeter. Exhaustive BFS from all 56 roots in two separately coded finite Fano models gives the unique shell vector (1,3,6,12,18,12,3,1), hence exact diameter seven; all checks executed from the included files. Finite checks are used only for the finite graph, not as proof of an infinite generalization.

value.rationale: The minimum three-path-cover problem is a natural graph-hitting and reconfiguration task; the Heawood Fano incidence graph is a canonical cubic six-cage. Its exact optimum-state geometry exhibits two frozen configurations and a highly structured mobile component identified with a classical symmetric graph, and it proves that local slides are no more restrictive than unrestricted jumps. This is a complete, motivated nontrivial structural characterization with exact reachability and worst-case routing information, rather than a small arbitrary parameter count.
